::: {#exr-gauss-score-fn}
#### Score function of a Gaussian variable

Derive the score function for a single Gaussian random variable $X$,
with respect to the mean parameter $\pmean$,
treating the variance $\ss$ as known.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-gauss-score-fn}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\score
&\eqdef \deriv{\pmean}\loglik
&& \text{(definition of the score)}\\
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{\frac{-1}{2}\paren{\logf{2\pi\ss} + \frac{(x - \pmean)^2}{\ss}}}
&& \text{(Gaussian log-likelihood)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\deriv{\pmean}\paren{\logf{2\pi\ss} + \frac{(x - \pmean)^2}{\ss}}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{\deriv{\pmean}\logf{2\pi\ss} + \deriv{\pmean}\frac{(x - \pmean)^2}{\ss}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{0 + \deriv{\pmean}\frac{(x - \pmean)^2}{\ss}}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{0 + \frac{1}{\ss}\deriv{\pmean}(x - \pmean)^2}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{0 + \frac{1}{\ss} \cdot 2(x - \pmean) \deriv{\pmean}(x - \pmean)}
&& \text{(chain rule, outer function $u^2$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The inner derivative is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\pmean}(x - \pmean)
&= \deriv{\pmean} x - \deriv{\pmean} \pmean
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 - \deriv{\pmean} \pmean
&& \text{($x$ does not depend on $\pmean$)}\\
&= 0 - 1
&& \text{(derivative of $\pmean$ with respect to itself)}\\
&= -1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the inner derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\score
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{0 + \frac{1}{\ss} \cdot 2(x - \pmean) \cdot (-1)}
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2}\paren{0 + \frac{-2(x - \pmean)}{\ss}}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{2} \cdot \frac{-2(x - \pmean)}{\ss}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}\\
&= \frac{x - \pmean}{\ss}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= \frac{x - \E{X}}{\ss}
&& \text{($\E{X} = \pmean$)}\\
&= \frac{x - \E{X}}{\Var{X}}
&& \text{($\Var{X} = \ss$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
